notes: _DStar per endpoint (planners dict, <=3, never rebuilt); replan() stops at k_min>=h(robot) OR perf_counter deadline (stop rule partial); seed() = MODIFY-COST re-OPENs CLOSED cells; _carrot follows pl.path backpointers, _choose_dir scores headings w/o forward sim; _start_recovery backs up + spins; cold start steers at goal

_DStar.reset_tree() called from _step when trace() finds corrupted backpointers (fallback, rate-limited 3 s); _run_planner stops at kmin>=h(target) OR budget/max_exp (partial); cell_cost_changed = MODIFY-COST; heading scored near traced plan w/o forward sim; _escape backs up + spins

_replan gated on REPLAN_EVERY steps or force_plan; _solve = vectorised Bellman sweeps from np.full INF each time; _build_candidates meshgrid + forward-integrated rollouts scored by value field at endpoint in _control; scripted recovery (rec_t1/rec_t2: reverse then turn to _escape_dir)

_step replans when force_replan or step_i-last_plan_step >= PLAN_EVERY; _plan relaxes D from np.full BIG (vectorised _relax sweeps); _choose scores precomputed arc rollouts (rx, ry) by progress on D; mode 'rec' (_start_recovery) drives toward an open bearing for rec_T s, stamps penalty, forces replan

one h field per goal key kept in self.fields and repaired each step by _sweep (vectorised RAISE = set inf where h < neighbour min, then LOWER = min-relax), fixed sweep counts per step; no from-scratch rebuild except _new_field for a new goal key (excluded); no k, no OPEN list, no stop rule; cost changes (_rebuild_cost) only add sweep credits globally (modify_cost partial); _path_points/_lookahead descend h (backpointers partial); recover_until mode drives away + spins

_replan every plan_period steps (next_plan gate): _sweep starts from np.full INF (fast-sweeping min-plus), _descend gives a path; dynamic window over precomputed arc rollouts (cX, cY) scored by carrot distance + field at endpoint; recover_until override spins/backs, adds penalty

one h field per goal key (self.fields), seeded once with straight-line bound in _ensure_field (new goal only, excluded) then _repair = budgeted vectorised Bellman sweeps (_relax) reusing h every step; no k / OPEN / stop rule (perf_counter budget only); RAISE and LOWER merged in one min-update; cost map rebuilt globally in _build_cost (modify_cost partial); _lookahead descends h; _local scores headings w/o forward sim; escape_until manoeuvre reverses + rotates

_plan_tick: anytime from-scratch build (Dbuild = np.full BIG, _relax sweeps amortised over steps), swapped into self.D when stable, then Dbuild=None so the next tick restarts from scratch (sliced search restarted = full_periodic); fields cached per goal; _plan_dir descends D to a lookahead heading, candidate headings scored by alignment+clearance w/o forward sim; _trigger_recovery mode + blockpen, drops the cached field

_plan_tick: wavefront started from scratch in _start_wave (Dw = np.full BIG), relaxed under perf_counter budget, _promote()d to Dact on convergence then Dw=None so the next tick restarts; field_cache per goal; directions scored by field sampled at straight-line lookahead points (no twist forward sim); _recover rec_mode 1 back away / 2 spin / 3 dither. RATER SAW THIS FILE'S HEADER BEFORE BLINDING (recognised)

_plan called when not plan_ok / no path / t-t_plan > PLAN_DT / _path_invalid; builds dist/D from np.full INF each time (vectorised sweeps); _lookahead + _choose scores heading offsets around phi_des by clearance w/o forward sim; mode 'backup' (_escape_direction) reverses / spins, stuck bumps penalty and forces replan

_Field per goal (h,k,t,b,OPEN heap), _process_state = L1-L26; _seed_pending = MODIFY-COST re-OPENs CLOSED cells + neighbours; _run_dstar stops at kmin>=h(robot) OR perf_counter deadline / max_exp (partial); inactive field deleted in _push_dirty if pending>120000 and rebuilt only when its goal returns (reinit_on_goal_switch, excluded); robot drives by _descend over decreasing h, not the b pointers (backpointers partial); _track = heading P-control to a path target; _escape_cmd backs away + spins

_plan_tick starts a fresh wave (_start_plan: D = np.full BIG) when forced / no D / PLAN_PERIOD elapsed, relaxes it over steps, publishes intermediates; _choose scores precomputed (vx,vy,wz) rollouts (_tp, endpoints _epx/_epy) by progress on D + clearance; _enter_recovery/_recover_cmd back off + spin, penalty, force replan

_plan_start (on force_replan or PLAN_PERIOD) builds a fresh coarse cost grid and a new heapq Dijkstra (pd = [INF]*nn), _plan_run pops a budgeted number per step; _carrot gives a heading, candidate directions scored by heading+clearance w/o forward sim; mode 'back' then 'spin' on stuck/contact

one h grid kept on the instance, cached per goal in hcache and restored in _switch_goal (np.full only when a goal has no cache = goal-switch init, excluded); _vi = vectorised full Bellman assignment named PROCESS-STATE, run vi_per_step per step or as a perf_counter-bounded _vi_burst; no k / OPEN / stop rule; RAISE and LOWER merged in one assignment; cost changes via global _rebuild_cost (modify_cost partial); _carrot descends h; _drive scores headings w/o forward sim; on stall rec_until mode steers to the freest direction (rec_target) and raises pen

_DStar per endpoint (planners), process_state L1-L25, modify_cost re-OPENs CLOSED cells, repair() stops at kmin>=h(start) OR perf_counter budget / max_exp (partial); the ONLY from-scratch path: every 37 steps, if the goal cell has become lethal a NEW _DStar is built on a relocated free goal cell (coded as fallback; narrow trigger, flag for rater 2); _path follows b; carrot heading P-control; escape_until mode drives a carrot toward the most open sector / straight back on contact

BORDERLINE (full_periodic vs incremental_with_fallback): one h field per goal kept in self.fields, but any newly occupied cell marks every field dirty and _work_field then _reset_field()s it to INF and regrows it from scratch (map-changed gate = full_periodic); only cost DECREASES are propagated incrementally (2 LOWER sweeps when settled); no k / OPEN; RAISE handled by reset, not propagated; 'Property 2 analogue' publishes h once h(robot) stops moving (stop rule partial); heading = argmin of field sampled on a ring (no b pointers); escape_until steers to freest direction + contact recovery_until backs away

planner_type: _DStar keeps h/k/b/OPEN across steps. _drive repairs it every step with pl.replan, and _seed_all feeds it the changed cells. The only new _DStar instance is created in _planner_for, when the goal key changes or a cached planner is evicted. That is reinit_on_goal_switch, which the rubric excludes from fallback. The stuck path (add_penalty then _seed_all) is an incremental repair, not a restart. The only discard-and-recompute route is the eviction of the least-recently-used planner, which comes back only as a goal switch. map: _GridMap holds a log-odds grid on the instance (update_scan, _transitions) and is not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: the nominal path is _carrot, which follows the D* backpointer path from pl.path, and then _choose_dir. _choose_dir scores 72 heading candidates by alignment, clearance and smoothness with no forward simulation, so it is path_following, not rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _start_recovery and the recovery block in _drive send their own commands (back up, rotate in place). That outranks the planning-level add_penalty step. D* checklist: Stentz 1994 form. insert() and min_state() order the heap on (k, x). process_state() separates RAISE (kold < h) from LOWER (kold >= h) and propagates each. seed() is MODIFY-COST: it re-inserts closed states with k = h. replan() stops when k_min >= h(robot) or OPEN is empty, but it also returns on a wall-clock deadline (perf_counter budget), which can end repair before the stopping rule holds, so ds_stop_rule is partial. Backpointers b[] are set in process_state and followed by path().

planner_type: _DStar trees persist across steps (self.planners). _drain_dirty -> cell_cost_changed repairs only affected states, and _run_planner calls process_state to repair. This is the nominal path. In _step, when pl.trace reports a corrupted backpointer sequence, pl.reset_tree() throws the search state away and rebuilds it (rate-limited by last_hard_reset). That is an inconsistency-triggered from-scratch fallback, so incremental_with_fallback. _get_planner creates a new tree for a new goal, and the cache keeps up to 3 trees; this is reinit_on_goal_switch and is excluded from the fallback test. Initialisation in reset() is also excluded. map: _update_map and _recompute_cost keep a log-odds grid (self.lo) and a cost grid (self.cost2d) on the instance across steps. The goal switch in _step only clears hist and escape_until, so the grid is not cleared on a goal switch. velocity_selection: the heading target th_des comes from the _step backpointer trace plus _los lookahead. The beam scoring that follows (score over sang with cos(dev) and clearance) ranks existing lidar beams against that heading. It does not forward-simulate any twist over a horizon, so it is path_following with a safety layer (_gate), not rollout_scored. stuck_handling: livelock detection and the contact handler in _step set escape_until, and the _escape method issues its own back-up and spin commands. That is a dedicated manoeuvre. explicit_recovery outranks the _raise_visited cost-raise, which alone would be timeout. D* checklist (Stentz 1994, by the paper's names): the heap in insert/get_kmin is keyed on (k, x). h, k, b and tag t are stored per state. process_state separates the RAISE case (k_old < h) from LOWER (h <= k_old) and handles them in separate branches, following the paper's L4-L25. cell_cost_changed re-inserts CLOSED states for the MODIFY-COST step, and _drain_dirty feeds it the changed cells and their neighbours. ds_stop_rule is partial: _run_planner implements 'k_min >= h(robot)' or OPEN empty, but also stops on max_exp and a wall-clock budget (0.013 s or 0.0055 s), so repair can end before the stopping rule holds. Backpointers b are set in process_state and followed by trace to drive the robot.

planner_type: _replan rebuilds the whole cost-to-go field from scratch via _solve (relaxation sweeps, goal pinned at 0, no state reused). It is gated in _control by `force_plan or (k - plan_k) >= REPLAN_EVERY` (12 steps), so full_periodic. force_plan is also set by _new_leg and by the stuck branch. map: self.lo is a log-odds grid updated in _update_map and kept on the instance across steps (reset() creates it; _new_leg only decays self.pen, it does not clear lo). A second grid, self.pen, holds remembered dead-end penalties. velocity_selection: _control scores the precomputed rollout candidates (_build_candidates, K sampled twists, 4 substeps over HORIZON 0.8 s) against lidar clearance and the value field, then takes argmin of cost. This is rollout_scored. The value field is used only inside the scoring, and _descend supplies the target. stuck_handling: the stuck branch in _control triggers on a progress window, no improvement in best_v, or contact count. It starts the scripted recovery (rec_t1/rec_t2): back up, rotate toward _escape_dir, then drive. It also adds penalties and forces a replan. A dedicated manoeuvre exists, so explicit_recovery takes precedence over timeout. claims_dstar: no D*, Stentz, LPA*, rhs, k_m, RAISE or LOWER vocabulary appears anywhere in the file, so all checklist items are na. Goal switch is handled in _new_leg and is not a fallback, since the planner is not incremental.

planner_type: _plan rebuilds a wavefront distance field D from scratch (np.full BIG, seed at goal, _relax loop) and is gated in _step by force_replan or step_i - last_plan_step >= period (PLAN_EVERY=20 / PLAN_EVERY_FAIL=8), plus a wall-clock budget; no state is reused across plans, so full_periodic. map: self.log log-odds grid updated in _map_update and kept on the instance across steps (also self.pen penalty grid); reset() allocates it once, not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: _choose forward-simulates 126 candidate (vx,vy,wz) arcs (rx/ry/rth precomputed over horizon T up to 1.2 s), scores clearance, progress and the global D field, and picks the argmax, so rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _start_recovery sets mode 'rec' and drives rec_u for rec_T seconds, plus the R_PANIC branch in _step backs off and rotates, so explicit_recovery wins over timeout-style force_replan and _stamp. claims_dstar: no D*/Stentz/LPA*/rhs/k_m/RAISE/LOWER vocabulary; 'D' is a wavefront distance array and _relax is a Bellman-Ford style sweep, so all checklist items na.

planner_type: per-goal h fields persist in self.fields across steps. _step runs _sweep every step, which repairs the stored h in place: a raise pass sets inconsistent cells to inf, then a lower pass relaxes. Stuck only adds sweep budget (burst, raise_debt) and scars; it never discards a field. _new_field is called only from reset() and when obs.goal gives an unseen key, so that is reinit_on_goal_switch, which is excluded from fallback. The 'eviction when more than 4 fields' branch in _new_field is also goal-keyed. The map is persistent_grid: self.logodds is a log-odds grid updated by _update_map and kept across steps; _rebuild_cost derives the cost grid from it. self.scar is persistent too. velocity_selection: on the nominal path, _path_points does greedy descent of h (backpointer-style), _lookahead picks a carrot, and _choose_dir scores 60 heading candidates by heading error, smoothness and static clearance, with no forward simulation. That makes it path_following, not rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _step sets recover_until after a displacement test and then issues a dedicated back-up and spin command (the 'recovery' block). There is also an emergency back-off when rmin < 0.30 and an all_blocked back-off. explicit_recovery outranks the timeout-style scarring. D* checklist, coded as Stentz 1994 because the code uses h, RAISE and LOWER vocabulary but no k: (1) There is no OPEN list or k. State is a dense array h, relaxed by vectorised Bellman sweeps (_nmin and _sweep), so open_keyed_on_k = no. (2) Only h is stored, with no k, so h_and_k = partial. (3) _sweep has separate raise (invalidate when h < nmin) and lower (h = min(h, nmin)) phases, not PROCESS-STATE's k<h versus k=h propagation, so raise_lower = partial. (4) _rebuild_cost recomputes the whole cost grid and sets raise_debt only when the lethal set changes. Nothing is re-inserted on OPEN, and non-lethal cost changes get no raise pass, so modify_cost = partial. (5) Repair uses a fixed per-step sweep budget (SWEEPS_ACTIVE + credits) and has no k_min >= h(robot) test, so stop_rule = no. (6) _path_points follows the argmin of h plus a tiny tie-break matrix (_dmat) rather than c + h, recomputed from the repaired field each step, so backpointers = partial.

planner_type: _replan() discards Dfield/Cplan/path and rebuilds the cost grid (_make_cost) and the cost-to-go field from scratch (_sweep, a fast-sweeping min-plus pass, not a priority-queue search). It is gated in _step by `self.k >= self.next_plan`, which is a timer (plan_period) plus forced replans from the stall and livelock detectors, and the goal switch only sets next_plan. Any gate puts this in full_periodic, so it is not full_every_step. No search state survives between replans, so it is not incremental. map: self.L is a log-odds occupancy grid written by _update_map from lidar and kept on the instance across steps; self.pen is a persistent penalty grid. The grid is kept across goal switches (the goal-switch block in _step does not clear L), so the note grid_cleared_on_goal_switch does not apply. Only pen is scaled by 0.30 on a goal switch. The goal-switch reset of path/Dfield and next_plan in _step is a new search for the new leg (reinit_on_goal_switch). velocity_selection: in _step, the 'dynamic window' block builds candidate (vx,vy,wz) twists (_build_candidates precomputes K=5 forward-simulated arc positions cX/cY over a 0.22 s step). It scores them against obstacle distance, carrot distance and the cost-to-go field, then takes the argmin. The rubric's rollout_scored line covers scoring against a global field. stuck_handling: the 'recovery override' block in _step issues dedicated back-up and rotate-in-place commands, triggered by the stall detector (stuck_count/recover_until) and by contact. Explicit recovery outranks the timeout-style penalties (_add_penalty, next_plan reset). claims_dstar: no identifier or comment names D*, Stentz, LPA*, RAISE/LOWER, rhs or k_m. 'Dfield' is a distance field, not a D* reference, so all checklist items are na.

planner_type: _ensure_field creates a per-goal h field, and _repair/_relax then keep updating that same h array across steps (_step calls _repair every step) as _build_cost changes the costs. Previous values are reused, so this is incremental. The field is never discarded and recomputed from scratch on stuck, no-path or timer triggers. The stuck branch in _step only stamps visit/obstacle costs. The only new-field path is a new goal key, plus LRU eviction in _ensure_field, so it counts as reinit_on_goal_switch (fields cached per endpoint, so the return trip reuses the old field). It is a hand-rolled Bellman-sweep equivalent that relaxes the whole grid rather than only affected states. map: logodds/seen/visit grids on the instance, written in _integrate_scan; no grid clearing on goal switch. velocity_selection: _lookahead traces steepest descent on h to a carrot point, and _local scores about 26 candidate headings by free distance along a ray (fd) without forward-simulating them, so it is path_following (heading offsets, not rollouts). stuck_handling: _step has an escape manoeuvre (back up, then rotate, driven by escape_until and escape_phase) triggered by the stalled/wedged tests; _local also has a boxed-in rotate-and-creep-back branch. This outranks the timeout-style cost stamping. D*: claims_dstar is yes from comments naming MODIFY-COST, Sec. 5.2, RAISE/LOWER, backpointers and Fig. 5/Property 2. The h vocabulary is Stentz-style but there is no k and no OPEN list. Checklist: ds_open_keyed_on_k is no because there is no OPEN list (_relax is a dense Bellman sweep). ds_h_and_k is partial because only h is stored, with no k. ds_raise_lower is partial because _relax docstring says raises and lowers alike, merged into one min-sweep with no k<h / k=h distinction. ds_modify_cost is partial because _integrate_scan, _build_cost and _stamp_obstacle change arc costs, but nothing re-inserts the affected states; the next sweep picks the change up everywhere. ds_stop_rule is no because _repair runs a fixed iteration count or time budget with no k_min >= h(robot) test. ds_backpointers is yes because _lookahead recomputes steepest-descent successors from h, which is the argmin analogue and is what drives the robot.

planner_type: _plan_tick builds a fresh cost-to-go field Dbuild (all _BIG, goal=0) and runs _relax (Bellman-Ford style sweeps) over several steps. When the field is stable or max_iters is reached it is swapped in and Dbuild=None, so the next tick restarts from scratch. This is a sliced search that restarts on completion, which the rubric codes as full_periodic. The only reuse of old values is the per-goal cache self.fields on goal switch. That cache is not a repair of changed costs, and the build still starts from scratch. _trigger_recovery also discards the field. map: self.logodds is a log-odds grid updated by _integrate and kept on the instance, so persistent_grid. It is not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: on the nominal path _plan_dir descends the cost-to-go field with a 1.0 m carrot lookahead to get phi_des. _step then scores 48 candidate headings (alignment, clearance, hysteresis) with no forward simulation, so path_following and not rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _trigger_recovery sets recover_until, which gives a dedicated rotate/creep command branch in _step. _on_contact sets evade_until, which gives a back-away command. It also adds blockpen, but explicit_recovery takes precedence over timeout. claims_dstar: no D*, Stentz, LPA*, rhs, k_m, RAISE or LOWER vocabulary appears. The D and Dbuild identifiers are plain distance fields, so every checklist item is na.

planner_type: _plan_tick/_start_wave/_promote. A min-plus wavefront cost-to-go field is rebuilt from scratch: _start_wave allocates Dw filled with _BIG and _seed_goal seeds the goal. The relaxation is time-sliced (PLAN_BUDGET) over several steps, then _promote sets Dw=None so the next step restarts from scratch. No values are reused after a cost change. The rubric puts a sliced search that restarts on completion in full_periodic. The budget gate and the convergence/iteration-cap gate also fit full_periodic. _on_goal_change reuses a cached field per goal (field_cache) but does not repair. map: self.log log-odds grid is written by _update_map, kept on the instance, and not cleared on goal change. velocity_selection: _step scores 61 candidate headings with a cost that samples the global field Dact at two straight-line lookahead points (_sample). Each heading is a geometric projection, not a forward-simulated (v,w) twist over a horizon. The command is then built from the chosen heading (phi -> vx, vy, wz). By the rubric's rule that heading offsets without forward simulation count as path_following, I coded path_following. It consults the field, so it is not reactive. This is the least clear-cut label. stuck_handling: the stuck watchdog in _step triggers _recover, which has back-up (mode 1), spin in place (mode 2) and dither near the goal (mode 3). That is explicit_recovery, which outranks the timeout-style _mark_stuck_spot. claims_dstar: no D*, D-star, Stentz, LPA*, rhs, k_m or RAISE/LOWER vocabulary appears. self.k is only a step counter. All checklist items are na.

planner_type: _plan() recomputes a wavefront cost-to-go from scratch via _wave() with no state reuse. It is gated in _step() by `need` (not plan_ok, path None, t - t_plan > PLAN_DT, _path_invalid), so full_periodic. map: _update_map() writes a log-odds grid self.log that is kept on the instance and grown by _ensure(); the grid is not cleared on goal switch, though self.pen is halved (pen *= 0.5). velocity_selection: the nominal command comes from _lookahead() (path pursuit with string-pulling via _los), then _choose() picks among OFFS heading offsets scored by _clearance without forward simulation. The rubric says a handful of heading offsets without forward simulation is still path_following. stuck_handling: _step() has a 'backup' mode with its own commands (back up or rotate in place), triggered by contact, _stuck(), or being boxed in, and explicit_recovery outranks the timeout-style _bump_penalty / forced replan. claims_dstar: no D* vocabulary (no RAISE/LOWER, rhs, k_m, Stentz, LPA*); the code only uses a wavefront and descent (_descend), so every checklist item is na. goal switch handling resets the path and forces replan in _step() (reinit_on_goal_switch); this is irrelevant for the full planner.

planner_type: _step section 3 keeps one _Field (h, k, t, b, OPEN) per goal in self._fields across steps. _refresh_cost and _push_dirty add changed cells to F.pending, and _seed_pending plus _run_dstar repair only those states. No path discards the current field and recomputes it. _push_dirty only deletes non-current fields whose pending set exceeds 120000, and _Field() is only built when no field exists for the goal, which is the goal-switch case, so it is not a fallback. Coded reinit_on_goal_switch (fields are kept per goal and a new one is built on a first visit). map: persistent_grid, from lo/occ/cost arrays written in _update_map and kept on the instance. _clear_penalties only clears the penalty layer, not the grid. velocity_selection: nominal path is _step section 5 (_descend along decreasing h, then _target_on_path), then _track, which is a heading P-controller toward the target plus a repulsion term and a slow-down. No forward simulation, so path_following. The reactive branch only runs when target is None. stuck_handling: _step section 4 detects lack of progress (5 s history span, contact counter) and sets _escape_until. _escape_cmd then issues its own commands (back away from the nearest obstacle while spinning in place), so explicit_recovery wins over the penalty/timeout part (_add_penalty). D* checks: variant is stentz1994 (h/k/t/b, RAISE/LOWER L-line comments in _process_state). ds_open_keyed_on_k: the heap in _insert and _kmin is keyed on k with lazy deletion. ds_h_and_k: yes, both are stored and k is updated on (re)insertion in _insert. ds_raise_lower: _process_state separates kold < h (RAISE) from kold == h (LOWER) and propagates each. ds_modify_cost: _seed_pending re-inserts the affected CLOSED states and their neighbours on OPEN. Seeding is rate-limited per step but the remainder stays pending. ds_stop_rule: partial, because _run_dstar tests k_min >= h(robot) but also stops on max_exp and a wall-clock deadline (budget_s), so repair can end before the rule holds. ds_backpointers: partial. b is updated in _process_state, but driving uses _descend, which takes argmin over neighbours of h + c rather than following b.

planner_type: _plan_tick/_start_plan rebuild the cost grid and reset the value field D from scratch (goal cells = 0, rest = BIG), then _relax runs value-iteration sweeps sliced over several steps. A new search starts only when the PLAN_PERIOD timer (0.7 s) expires or _force_plan is set (by _enter_recovery or _new_leg). That is gated and restarts from scratch each time, so full_periodic, not incremental. map: self.logodds is a persistent log-odds grid written in _update_map and kept across steps; it is not cleared on goal switch (_new_leg only resets D). velocity_selection: _choose forward-simulates 80 candidate twists over a 1.3 s horizon (precomputed trajectories in _build_candidates), scores them against clearance and the global cost field D, and sends the best; so rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _is_stuck and the 16 s no-progress test trigger _enter_recovery; _recover_cmd backs up and rotates in place, and _bump_cmd backs away after contact. These are dedicated manoeuvres, so explicit_recovery beats timeout. claims_dstar: no D*, Stentz, LPA*, rhs, RAISE/LOWER or k_m vocabulary appears. The planner is value iteration over a grid, so all checklist items are na.

planner_type: _plan_start builds a fresh cost grid and a fresh Dijkstra (new pd/heap) from the goal, and _plan_run slices it over steps. _step gates it with PLAN_PERIOD, force_replan (goal switch, pose jump, stuck, _carrot hitting an INF cell) and pl_active. No state is reused across searches, so this is full_periodic. map: self.lo log-odds grid updated in _update_map and kept on the instance; the grid is not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: nominal path in _step takes a lookahead point from _carrot, which descends the cost-to-go field, then picks a heading among 72 candidate directions by heading, clearance and previous-direction score. Nothing is forward-simulated (_clearance is a geometric corridor check), so this is path_following, not rollout_scored. Near-goal dither only moves the target. stuck_handling: _step stall/contact detection switches to mode 'back' then 'spin', each with its own commands, so explicit_recovery wins over the timeout-style _add_penalty. claims_dstar: no D* identifiers or vocabulary; the only search is Dijkstra, so all checklist items are na. reinit_on_goal_switch does not apply because the planner is not incremental.

planner_type: self.h is kept across steps and updated by _vi(), a vectorised full-Bellman sweep, a few iterations per step in _step. There is no code path that discards h and recomputes, so incremental_only. The only reset is the new h in _switch_goal, which may reload cached h; note reinit_on_goal_switch. A stall calls _rebuild_cost and, every third time, _vi_burst, but neither clears h, so neither counts as a fallback. The repair is a whole-grid sweep, not an affected-states-only repair, which I accept as a hand-rolled equivalent. map: self.lo (log-odds) and self.seen are filled by _integrate and persist on the instance; the grid is not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: on the nominal path _carrot() follows steepest descent on h to a carrot point, and _drive() then picks among 48 heading candidates by a static score (clearance, goal bearing, previous heading) with no forward simulation, so path_following. stuck_handling: _step sets recovering/rec_target via contact and stall detection, and _drive then overrides the heading and caps speed (v<=0.32), a dedicated recovery mode. The stall branch also raises self.pen costs (timeout style), but explicit_recovery wins on precedence. D* checklist: the comments use PROCESS-STATE, MODIFY-COST, RAISE and LOWER, so claims_dstar is yes.
